harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built the double-NAT path (node3/lan-a -> node1 -> transit -> node2 -> node4/lan-b:8080) so node4 records the connection as arriving from node2's lan-b address. Then executed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes, confirming boot-identity change and full recovery (config, services, and end-to-end connectivity) after each restart.
actions_performed: Discovered physical topology by testing candidate subnets across unconfigured interfaces: lan-a = node1 eth2 <-> node3 eth1; transit = node1 eth1 <-> node2 vtnet1; lan-b = node2 vtnet2 <-> node4 eth1

Configured node1 (VyOS): addressed eth1=10.10.2.1/24 (transit) and eth2=10.10.1.254/24 (lan-a); added static route 10.10.3.0/24 via 10.10.2.2; added source NAT rule 10 (masquerade on eth1 for source 10.10.1.0/24); added forward-filter default-drop plus established/related, tcp/8080, and icmp accept rules; committed and saved

Configured node2 (OPNsense) via config.xml Python surgery: added opt1 (vtnet1, 10.10.2.2/24 transit) and opt2 (vtnet2, 10.10.3.254/24 lan-b) interfaces; added pf pass rules for tcp/8080 and icmp on opt1; switched outbound NAT to hybrid mode and added manual SNAT masquerading 10.10.2.0/24 traffic out opt2; applied via configctl interface reconfigure + configctl filter reload without losing SSH/exec reachability
Configured node3 (10.10.1.10/24 on eth1, persisted in /etc/network/interfaces with a static route to 10.10.3.0/24 via node1) and node4 (10.10.3.10/24 on eth1, persisted similarly)
Installed busybox-extras and tcpdump on node4; started an httpd service on port 8080 serving a test page, made persistent via /etc/local.d/httpd8080.start + rc-update add local default

Verified end-to-end: node3 fetched http://10.10.3.10:8080 successfully; tcpdump on node4 eth1 and node4's socket table showed source 10.10.3.254 (node2 lan-b IP), not node1 or node3; conntrack on node1 and pf state on node2 confirmed both NAT hops
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id/kern.boottime + service/config state) on all 4 nodes

Restarted node3, node4, node1, node2 one at a time via native reboot, polling exec availability, confirming changed boot identity, and re-verifying config/service recovery and the full double-NAT path after each restart

evidence.summary: Bidirectional ping tests across distinct test subnets on the spare interfaces established that node1 eth2<->node3 eth1 (lan-a), node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 (transit), and node2 vtnet2<->node4 eth1 (lan-b)

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) NAT + firewall + routing configuration applied
evidence.summary: show interfaces/ip route/nat source rules/firewall confirm eth1/eth2 addressing, static route to lan-b, masquerade SNAT rule 10, and forward-filter rules are active

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) interface/NAT/firewall configuration applied without losing exec access
evidence.summary: config.xml updated, opt1/opt2 reconfigured with correct IPs, filter reload succeeded (SSH still reachable), pfctl -s nat shows the manual SNAT rule on vtnet2, pfctl -s rules shows pass rules for tcp/8080 and icmp on vtnet1

evidence.requirement: node3/node4 addressing and lan-b HTTP service in place
evidence.summary: eth1 addresses and routes configured on node3/node4; httpd installed and listening on node4:8080

evidence.requirement: End-to-end connection succeeds and node4 records source as node2's lan-b address (core task requirement)
evidence.summary: node3 successfully fetched the page from node4:8080; tcpdump on node4's eth1 and its netstat socket table show the incoming SYN/connection sourced from 10.10.3.254 (node2 lan-b IP); conntrack on node1 and pf state on node2 show both NAT translation hops (10.10.1.10->10.10.2.1 then 10.10.2.1->10.10.3.254)

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 48193c62...; reboot acked; connection dropped confirming restart in progress; new boot_id ae0b9e32... with uptime 0 min; post-restart eth1/route/wget to node4:8080 all recovered

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a36fc7f5... with httpd listening; reboot acked; new boot_id 7750af4c... uptime 0 min; eth1 address and httpd service auto-recovered via local.d; node3 successfully re-fetched the page confirming full path recovery

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e636d872...; reboot acked; new boot_id fd14b431... uptime 0 min; VyOS NAT rule and full route table (including static route to lan-b) restored from saved config; node3 successfully re-fetched the page confirming recovery

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state, full path re-verified post-all-restarts
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 04:34:21; reboot acked (SSH connection timed out confirming restart); new kern.boottime 04:45:30; opt1/opt2 interfaces, SNAT rule, and pf pass rules all restored from config.xml; final tcpdump on node4 after all 4 restarts shows the connection still sourced from 10.10.3.254, proving the double-NAT path is fully persistent and functional
